series: Promo bank, built Oct 7, 2026 for CMO review
hook: A $150 booth fee is really $315.60 for the day
hook_say: Here is what a $150 craft fair booth really costs once the drive, meals and display come in, and how many pieces pay for it.

rows.label: Booth fee
rows.why: The calculator's example show: a $150 booth fee for a 7-hour day.

rows.label: Miles, meals, extras, display
rows.why: 60 miles round trip at 76 cents is $45.60, plus $25 organizer extras, $10 parking, $20 meals, $15 other and a $50 share of this year's display.

rows.label: What the day really costs
rows.why: Total fixed show cost: $315.60. The booth fee is only 48% of it.

rows.label: Each piece clears
rows.why: Across the five example products, a blended piece sells for $13.84 and clears $6.24 after materials, making time, packaging and the card fee.

rows.label: Pieces to break even
rows.why: $315.60 divided by $6.24, rounded up: 51 pieces, or $705.84 of sales, before the day makes a cent.

rows.label: Soy candle price
rows.why: The candle sits under the x2 price check at $22. Raise it to $26.

fix.label: Pieces to break even now
fix.why: Same day, same costs: the break-even drops from 51 pieces to 44.

cta.title: Craft Fair Profit Calculator
cta.say: Search ProofNotFluff for the full workbook.

note: Example numbers from the calculator. Yours go in the yellow cells.

sources.source: 1 Show Costs D18 (booth fee, example input)
1 Show Costs H7, costs on top of the booth fee: I15 25 + I16 45.60 (D20 60 mi x D21 0.76) + I17 10 + I19 20 + I21 50 (D26 300 / D27 6) + I22 15
1 Show Costs I23 and C7, total fixed show cost
1 Show Costs C8, 'The $150 booth fee is 48% of it'
2 Products H8 = 6.237672, contribution per piece (blended by the Mix column); 3 Break-Even D18
2 Products C8, blended price per piece
3 Break-Even I14 and C7, pieces you must sell
2 Products G25 (soy candle price 22, example); O25 'below formula'; state 2 sets G25 = 26
3 Break-Even I14 with 2 Products G25 = 26 (sales I15 $652.96)
